To find the ratio of silicon atoms in the photospheres of Star_1 and Star_2, we interpret the given bracketed abundances using the standard definition: [X/Y] = log₁₀(X/Y)ₛₜₐᵣ − log₁₀(X/Y)☉. The ratio of silicon atoms is taken as the ratio of their Si/H abundances, i.e. (n_Si/n_H)₁ / (n_Si/n_H)₂.

For **Star_1**:  
[Fe/H]₁ = 0 → [Fe/H]₁ = log(Fe/H)₁ − log(Fe/H)☉ = 0 ⇒ (Fe/H)₁ = (Fe/H)☉.  
[Si/Fe]₁ = 0.3 ⇒ [Si/H]₁ = [Si/Fe]₁ + [Fe/H]₁ = 0.3 + 0 = 0.3.  
Thus (Si/H)₁ = 10^{0.3} (Si/H)☉.

For **Star_2**:  
[Mg/H]₂ = 0 ⇒ (Mg/H)₂ = (Mg/H)☉.  
[Mg/Si]₂ = 0.3 ⇒ [Mg/Si]₂ = [Mg/H]₂ − [Si/H]₂ = 0.3 ⇒ 0 − [Si/H]₂ = 0.3 ⇒ [Si/H]₂ = −0.3.  
Thus (Si/H)₂ = 10^{−0.3} (Si/H)☉.

The ratio of silicon atoms (Si/H) is therefore:  
(Si/H)₁ / (Si/H)₂ = 10^{0.3} / 10^{−0.3} = 10^{0.6} ≈ 3.98 ≈ 3.9.

This corresponds to option (D).

**Answer: D**
